newsitem.title: USA: FCC denies Perot request for more TV prime time.
newsitem.headline: FCC denies Perot request for more TV prime time.

text.p: In another setback for Ross Perot, regulators said Friday they rejected a request by the Texan billionaire to force big television networks to sell him more prime time for his presidential campaign.

The Federal Communications Commission, in a 4 to 0 vote on a complaint filed last week by Perot, said the networks acted legally when they refused to sell the Reform Party candidate all the prime time slots he wanted for campaign infomercials.

Perot charged that ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox were unwilling to sell him "reasonable" air time in violation of a federal law ensuring that candidates have equal opportunity to appear on TV and "reasonable access" to the airwaves.

He cited, among other elements, the widespread coverage President Clinton and Republican Bob Dole received at their parties' nominating conventions in August, as well as the air time both will get in the upcoming presidential debates.
But the FCC said the networks were exempted from the equal opportunities provision of the law because the Clinton and Dole appearances cited by Perot were "bona fide" news events.
The agency said the networks had followed the proper procedure in deciding whether to grant Perot all of the nine half-hour prime time slots he requested from each network.
